title: Trust page: pick a layout
question: Built for judges first: they should 'get' the locked room in seconds. Which layout should the Trust page use? (Colors and fonts stay Air Check's; data shown is labeled Sample, taken from today's real sandbox tests.)

options.label: The rules, then the log
options.lineage: a building's posted access policy beside its door log
options.thesis: Show the allow-list in plain words next to everything the agent tried, so the locked room explains itself.
options.viewport: Desktop. A 'Waiting for you' bar on top. Left: 'What the agent is allowed to reach' with 4 destinations and why each exists, plus 'the agent holds no Box, Drive, Dropbox or Mixcloud keys'. Right: 'What it tried to reach', blocked first.
options.risk: Two panels compete; the log gets narrow columns.

options.label: One timeline
options.thesis: One honest stream of everything: what waits for you, what the agent did, where it reached, with filters.
options.viewport: Desktop. Filter chips (All · Waiting · Agent actions · Network · Blocked) over one wide table mixing actions and network requests in time order, blocked rows tinted red.
options.risk: Blocked events don't stand out as much for a judge skimming the video.

options.label: Incident reports
options.thesis: Each blocked attempt gets its own plain-language report card; routine traffic sits quietly below.
options.viewport: Desktop. Two report cards side by side: 'The agent tried to open example.com' and 'Hermes tried to contact its maker', each with program, destination, rule, outcome and one plain sentence. Below: 'Everything else it reached today'.
options.risk: On a quiet day with no blocks, the top of the page is empty.
